findings.title: Materials' 53-point lens gap signals earnings collapse
findings.body: Materials trades at 17.40x forward but 39.73x trailing, a 56 percent compression that analysts justify with 128 percent implied earnings growth. That is a bet on a dramatic profit recovery, yet the trailing multiple sits at the 94th percentile of its five-year range—the market is pricing in a rebound from an already expensive base.

findings.title: Consumer Staples' forward cheapness masks rich trailing
findings.body: Consumer Staples' forward P/E of 19.73 sits at the 35th percentile while its trailing multiple of 29.26 is at the 87th percentile, a 52-point gap. The market is underwriting 48 percent earnings growth, but the trailing valuation suggests investors are paying a premium for defensive stability that the forward lens says will evaporate.

findings.title: Utilities' month-long slide hits extreme cheapness
findings.body: Utilities' forward percentile dropped 32 points in one month to the 25th percentile, while its trailing multiple sits at the 11th percentile. The sector now trades at 17.59x forward with only 12 percent implied growth, a rare combination of low valuation and modest expectations that has not been this cheap in five years.
